subject: Physics
q: For an ideal gas of fixed number density, how does the mean free time $\tau$ between successive molecular collisions vary with absolute temperature T?
hint: Mean free time equals mean free path divided by a characteristic molecular speed.
solution: At fixed number density, the mean free path is constant, while the mean molecular speed is proportional to $\sqrt{T}$. Therefore $\tau=\lambda/\bar v\propto 1/\sqrt{T}$.
